title: "Residualizing a predictor"
execute:
  enabled: true
  echo: true
  warning: false

**Residualizing a predictor** subtracts the part linearly predicted by declared controls. The resulting residual is sample- and model-dependent; it is not a purified linguistic measurement.

## The MALD phone-count coefficient

First regress phone count on syllable count, log duration, and log frequency:

$$
P_i
=
\alpha_0+\alpha_sS_i+\alpha_dD_i+\alpha_fF_i+R_{Pi}.
$$

Then retain the same controls in the response model:

$$
Y_i
=
\gamma_0+\gamma_pR_{Pi}
+\gamma_sS_i+\gamma_dD_i+\gamma_fF_i+\varepsilon_i.
$$

The Frisch--Waugh--Lovell result implies that $\widehat\gamma_p$ equals the phone-count coefficient in the original multiple regression containing $P_i$ and the same controls.

```{r}
#| label: residualize-mald-phone-count
library(ggplot2)

mald <- read.csv("data/mald/mald-items.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
phone_residualizer <- lm(
  n_phones ~ n_syllables + log_duration + log_frequency_subtlex,
  data = mald
)
mald$residual_n_phones <- residuals(phone_residualizer)

original_fit <- lm(
  mean_log_rt ~ n_phones + n_syllables +
    log_duration + log_frequency_subtlex,
  data = mald
)
residualized_fit <- lm(
  mean_log_rt ~ residual_n_phones + n_syllables +
    log_duration + log_frequency_subtlex,
  data = mald
)

response_residualizer <- lm(
  mean_log_rt ~ n_syllables + log_duration + log_frequency_subtlex,
  data = mald
)
mald$residual_mean_log_rt <- residuals(response_residualizer)
partial_fit <- lm(residual_mean_log_rt ~ residual_n_phones, data = mald)

slope_difference <-
  coef(original_fit)[["n_phones"]] -
  coef(residualized_fit)[["residual_n_phones"]]

stopifnot(
  abs(slope_difference) < 1e-10,
  abs(
    coef(original_fit)[["n_phones"]] -
      coef(partial_fit)[["residual_n_phones"]]
  ) < 1e-10
)

data.frame(
  representation = c("original", "predictor residual", "both residuals"),
  phone_slope = c(
    coef(original_fit)[["n_phones"]],
    coef(residualized_fit)[["residual_n_phones"]],
    coef(partial_fit)[["residual_n_phones"]]
  )
)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-mald-residualization
#| fig-cap: "MALD response residuals against phone-count residuals. The line represents the same partial phone coefficient as the original multiple regression."
point_opacity <- 0.07
ggplot(mald, aes(residual_n_phones, residual_mean_log_rt)) +
  geom_point(color = "grey65", alpha = point_opacity, size = 0.55) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = FALSE,
    color = "#2C6E9B",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  labs(x = "Phone-count residual", y = "Mean log-RT residual") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

## Residualization inside validation folds

If residualized predictors are used for prediction, the residualizer must be fitted on training items only. Otherwise held-out predictor information leaks into preprocessing.

```{r}
#| label: validate-mald-foldwise-residualization
n_folds <- 10L
set.seed(20261020)
fold_id <- sample(rep(seq_len(n_folds), length.out = nrow(mald)))
fold_checks <- vector("list", n_folds)

for (fold in seq_len(n_folds)) {
  training <- fold_id != fold
  testing <- !training

  fold_residualizer <- lm(
    n_phones ~ n_syllables + log_duration + log_frequency_subtlex,
    data = mald[training, ]
  )
  train <- mald[training, ]
  test <- mald[testing, ]
  train$phone_residual <- residuals(fold_residualizer)
  test$phone_residual <- test$n_phones -
    predict(fold_residualizer, newdata = test)

  fold_original <- lm(
    mean_log_rt ~ n_phones + n_syllables +
      log_duration + log_frequency_subtlex,
    data = train
  )
  fold_residualized <- lm(
    mean_log_rt ~ phone_residual + n_syllables +
      log_duration + log_frequency_subtlex,
    data = train
  )

  fold_checks[[fold]] <- data.frame(
    fold = fold,
    maximum_prediction_difference = max(abs(
      predict(fold_original, newdata = test) -
        predict(fold_residualized, newdata = test)
    ))
  )
}
fold_checks <- do.call(rbind, fold_checks)
stopifnot(max(fold_checks$maximum_prediction_difference) < 1e-10)

fold_checks
```

The maximum foldwise prediction difference is `r format(max(fold_checks$maximum_prediction_difference), scientific = TRUE, digits = 2)`. This equality depends on retaining the same controls. Dropping them after residualization generally changes the fitted subspace and the estimand.

## Check your understanding

1. Why is the phone residual not a directly observed phonological property?
2. Which controls must be retained for the coefficient equivalence?
3. Why is full-data residualization leakage during validation?
4. What exactly agrees across the two foldwise models?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. The phone residual is the remainder from a sample-fitted linear model using syllables, duration, and frequency, so it depends on those controls and this MALD sample. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. The response model must retain syllable count, log duration, and log frequency, the same controls used in the phone residualizer. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. The full-data residualizer uses held-out predictor values to define the preprocessing transformation before prediction. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. The two models produce the same held-out fitted predictions within each fold, and their corresponding partial phone coefficients agree when the same controls are retained. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->

</details>
